questions.description: How accurately do resistance-training participants estimate repetitions to task failure?
questions.gap: Individual agreement and within-athlete calibration by task/load/effort not established.

questions.description: How do autoregulated load prescriptions affect strength compared with standardized loading?
questions.gap: Hybrid-specific outcomes and independent effects of adjustment parameters unknown.

questions.description: How do velocity-loss stopping thresholds affect strength and muscle size?
questions.gap: Realized repetition exposure differs; not weekly working-set adjustment.

questions.description: How does set structure and proximity to failure affect acute task performance and its recovery?
questions.gap: Individual recovery timing and concurrent-running transfer uncertain.

questions.description: How does HRV-guided endurance training affect measured outcomes compared with predefined training?
questions.gap: Incremental utility beyond performance and subjective feedback and hybrid efficacy untested.

questions.description: How does experimentally induced acute sleep loss affect exercise performance?
How do sleep observations from wearable devices agree with reference measurements?
questions.gap: Model/version-specific agreement not longitudinal sensitivity or intervention efficacy.

questions.description: How does an acute resistance-training session affect subsequent measures in runners?
questions.gap: Dose-specific kinetics, task specificity and individual scheduling efficacy unresolved.

questions.description: How should a coach review observations and propose bounded changes across disciplines?
questions.gap: No validated joint recovery score or incremental-benefit model; policy is candidate methodology.

methods.question: resistance-load-autoregulation
methods.description: Review comparable completed load and repetitions, optional anchored effort, task purpose and authorized bounds; permit hold, bounded changes or clarification.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: No exact RIR, automatic increment, or claim that adaptive rule is optimal.

methods.question: hybrid-recovery-methodology
methods.description: Review actual working sets, progression and local tolerance together with endurance demands; hold a productive dose or propose bounded redistribution or reduction.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: Velocity loss does not establish weekly set rule; local fatigue need not reduce all tasks.

methods.question: hybrid-recovery-methodology
methods.description: Separate eligible task-matched comparisons, qualitative observations and missing/ineligible data; ask targeted feedback when material to choice.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: Measurement agreement and responsiveness do not establish incremental utility; no composite readiness score.

methods.question: hybrid-recovery-methodology
methods.description: Protect priority sessions, consider local burden and competing explanations, and propose bounded calendar or dose changes rather than automatic rest.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: Endurance intervention is bundled and not direct hybrid evidence; secondary commitments need review.

methods.question: hybrid-recovery-methodology
methods.description: Use eligible autonomic and sleep observations as context, not deterministic readiness; exclude unknown units or protocol and retain other observations.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: Optional sensors; no universal thresholds or diagnostic inference; incremental value unverified.

methods.question: hybrid-recovery-methodology
methods.description: Review comparable outcomes and actual exposure, propose smallest feasible change consistent with objectives, revalidate restrictions and obtain approval; preserve history.
methods.provenance: Original candidate methodology, Research Packet 008 revision 0.1, sections 3–4.
methods.tradeoffs: Procedure is not proven efficacy; clinical restrictions and uncertainty override ordinary progression.
